claim: People hold and report only about 3 to 5 hypotheses at once, and skill does not raise the count (Mehle 3.4 vs 3.4 novice/expert; Elstein 3-5; HyGene working-memory 2 vs 4).
agent_test: Make the candidate list an external object; compare agent breadth with free-form list vs forced N>=6 at equal tokens.

claim: Pooled over people, the space of plausible causes is several times larger than any one person's list (17.8 distinct vs 3.4 each; one person found 19% of pool; pooling curve still rising at 12).
agent_test: Sample K independent generations at temperature, union them, measure new-cause yield per extra sample vs one long list. Model-side version now exists: see K20.

claim: Lists feel complete: stated probability that the true cause is on the list is ~68% while pooled estimates sum to 504%, and people shift only a little weight to 'all other' when branches are hidden (.078 expected .468, observed .140; experienced mechanics .215 vs .441).
agent_test: Show the agent a pruned vs full cause list; measure its 'other' mass. Add a forced 'what is not on this list' step and compare.

claim: Splitting a branch into finer detail raises its judged share (about +.066, about a third more) and lowers 'other'; the representation of the list shapes beliefs.
agent_test: Present the same hypothesis space as coarse vs fine; check if agent probability moves.

claim: Cognitive load or low working memory lowers the number of hypotheses generated and raises the sum of probabilities over exclusive hypotheses; the effect is mediated by count generated (small: sums 261.8 to 271.5, about +3.7% not the +10% the text claims).
agent_test: Vary context load (long distractor) and count candidates; test whether an external list removes the effect.

claim: Cue order shapes generation: later cues weigh more at slow presentation, earlier at fast; inconsistent hypotheses are purged, not re-cued.
agent_test: Permute cue order in agent prompts; measure final-top-1 change. Mixed result in Lange 2012 (no order effect on count, only weight).

claim: Supplying a list of hypotheses to physicians gives no clear consistent benefit and may bias: physicians whose initial diagnosis was on the list sought less info and changed less.
schema_part: G (no anchoring on supplied list), O
agent_test: Give agent a supplied hypothesis list with and without the true cause; measure info requests and switches. LLM analog: accepting a wrong supplied option is measured (K24) and biased test choice is measured (K25), but less information seeking after a supplied hypothesis is still unmeasured.

claim: Telling people about bias or training cognitive forcing does not reliably help: cognitive forcing gave no effect (52 vs 48% started a second search); availability-bias induction failed to replicate in residents (Staal 2021, N=117); guided reflection and tools give modest gains (d=0.38 and g=0.20, snippet only).
agent_test: Compare 'beware anchoring' prompt vs structural step (forced rival list) at equal tokens.

claim: First impressions/early hypotheses strongly steer later reasoning in humans (odds of cancer dx 4.9x with cancer first impression; Kostopoulou 2016, snippet).
agent_test: Inject a wrong early hypothesis into the agent context; measure recovery.

claim: LLMs show premature closure: on no-correct-option items they take a false action ~70% of the time at baseline, ~48% with a safety prompt (n=500 MedQA, 490 AfriMed); model spread 55-81%; reduction came with accuracy cost for some models (Grok 3). Second source: Bedi 2025 replaced the correct MedQA option with 'None of the other answers' on 68 items and all six models lost accuracy (drops 8.8 to 38.2 points; reasoning models least).
agent_test: Add a none-of-the-above option test to our harness; compare plain vs scaffold with an explicit 'is the true cause listed' check.

claim: LLM agents anchor on their round-1 diagnosis: 65.6% of wrong/partial round-1 diagnoses stayed wrong (212/323), and 50.8% of correct ones fell by round 3; information requests fall 7.5 to 1.8 per round. Second source (different task, ordinal triage): six LLMs stay tied to the chief-complaint exchange and generic reasoning prompts do not lift the plateau (best QWK 0.295 vs clinicians 0.887 to 0.929).
agent_test: Run a staged-information task; force at each stage a re-ranking from scratch vs carry-forward; compare.

claim: LLMs are better at the final diagnosis than at differential reasoning (gap 23.0 points) and a differential list often contains the answer when top-1 is wrong (78.3% in differential vs 52% first, NEJM).
agent_test: Score list-contains vs top-1 for plain and scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: Multi-role scaffolds improve LLM diagnosis: devil's advocate + facilitator agents moved GPT-4 from 0/80 initial to 71.3% top and 80% in top two; MAI-DxO 81.9% vs o3 78.6% and physicians 19.9%. Added 2025-2026 controls on general reasoning: five debate methods did not reliably beat CoT or self-consistency (Zhang 2025); at matched compute debate and mixture-of-agents beat self-consistency by only 1.3 to 2.7 points on MMLU-Pro. No diagnosis task has a same-token single-agent control.
agent_test: Run own control on a fault task: same total tokens, (a) one agent with self-consistency, (b) challenger scaffold. Score true-cause coverage and top-1.

claim: LLM access alone does not help physicians (Goh 2024: 76 vs 74, diff 2, CI -4 to 8) although the LLM alone scored 16 points higher; assistance helps in McDuff (51.7 vs 36.1).
agent_test: Not a direct agent test; shows an LLM list needs to be used. Note b23 and c08 are the same study.

claim: Human cognitive-bias tests transfer unevenly to LLMs: anchoring is strong when hints are given (162 comparisons, 11 exceptions), bias drops 10-26% in BiasMedQA (confirmation 0.2% for GPT-4), self-debiasing prompts can over-correct (Llama changed 40-52% of decisions). Added detail: Echterhoff change rates GPT-3.5 5.2%, GPT-4 17.5%, Llama-2-13b 52.1%, Llama-2-7b 39.9% (no ground truth, so over-correction is inferred). A prompt-level defense lifted GPT-4o a lot and Llama-8B almost not (Med-Stress).
agent_test: Test anchoring hint and self-debias prompt vs forced re-derivation at equal tokens.

claim: Agent designs that fix hypotheses early or commit as soon as they can answer score lower in RCA (GoS 48.2, OpenRCA 46.6 vs DiagGuard gain median +10.5); early trajectory similarity predicts failure (AUROC 0.81).
agent_test: Measure trajectory variability early as a stopping/fanout trigger.

claim: Retaining low-confidence hypotheses rather than dropping them is a design used in FVDebug (confidence<0.2 marked, not dropped); no ablation seen.
agent_test: Ablate dropping vs marking at equal tokens.

claim: A scaffold that forces a ranked differential at every stage with a documented reason for each removal stopped silent loss of a found diagnosis (unscaffolded kept it in 6/10 cases; scaffold 0 losses) but cut top-1 accuracy from 60% to 40% and access from 90% to 80%. Basis is a 10-case deep subset of 50 cases, one model, true cause in top 3 (Wang 2026, medRxiv). Earlier text 'zero regressions in 40 stage observations' omitted the top-1 cost.
agent_test: Log best-seen hypothesis; compare final answer vs best-seen. Run three arms at equal tokens: free-form update, ledger with removal reasons, from-scratch re-rank at each stage. Score retention and top-1.

claim: Slowing down is not clearly beneficial: correct diagnoses were faster than incorrect (115 vs 129 s, d=.37); confidence-accuracy R2=0.03.
agent_test: Check agent self-confidence vs accuracy calibration.

claim: Independent LLM samples are mostly repeats and the count of distinct hypotheses grows well below linearly in K. Induction task: unique programs among K=2,4,8,16,32 draws were 1.40, 1.79, 2.92, 4.56, 7.89 (GPT-4o-mini, failed instances). Differential diagnosis (302 NEJM cases): going from 1 to 5 independent draws raised recall of the reference differential concepts by only 0.131 on average. On enumerated hypothesis spaces, uniqueness and recovery fall as the space grows while validity stays high; duplicates are the main failure. This is the model-side Mehle curve, flatter than hoped.
agent_test: Measure new-distinct-cause yield per extra draw on our own fault tasks; compare to a single call that must name K distinct concepts first (K20/K21).

claim: A bare 'give something different from the earlier list' step did not raise coverage of true causes in differential diagnosis (chained vs independent draws at k=5: mean relative VTC -7.9%, positive in 1 of 8 configurations; per-draw precision fell). A concept-first structure (name K distinct concepts, then one hypothesis each) did add distinct hypotheses and 4.5 to 5.0 accuracy points at equal K in program induction. Task-dependent; not yet tested on fault causes.
schema_part: S1 generate by decomposition; ledger 'what is not listed' step
agent_test: At equal tokens compare: independent draws, chained exclusion list, concept-first list. Score true-cause coverage, not novelty.

claim: Forcing a differential-first few-shot prompt gave GPT-4 no reliable gain over plain chain of thought (76% vs 78%, +2.2, CI -1.4 to +5.8) and cost GPT-3.5 8 points (46% vs 38%) on 518 MedQA free-response items. Verified from the arXiv text; 2023 models; not re-tested on current models or non-medical faults.
agent_test: Re-run a differential-first instruction vs plain CoT on current models and a non-medical fault set; include a weak model.

claim: Models reliably under-use 'none of the listed': in Bedi 2025 replacing the correct option with NOTA cut accuracy for all six models (68 items; drops 8.8 to 38.2 points; reasoning models least) and in Handler 2026 false action on no-correct-option items was about 70% at baseline. No study tests a forced 'what is not on this list' ledger step against free-form lists.
agent_test: Build a NOTA fault set; arms: free list, list plus forced 'is the true cause missing' step, list plus independent re-sampling at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs accept a wrong supplied option and authority raises acceptance: expert-framed nudge cut accuracy 1.6 to 19.8 points across six models vs 0.3 to 7.5 for a plain nudge, and thinking Qwen-3 variants collapsed more than instruct variants (M42 2026). Multi-turn pressure makes models abandon correct diagnoses and a system-prompt defense worked for GPT-4o (41.50 to 92.79) but barely for Llama-8B (1.55 to 8.00) (Med-Stress 2026). Whether a supplied hypothesis makes an LLM seek less information is not measured.
schema_part: G (supplied hypothesis is a candidate, not a premise)
agent_test: Insert a wrong and a right supplied hypothesis into an agentic fault task; count information requests and switches with and without a forced refute-the-leader step.

claim: LLMs show confirmation bias in test choice: in a 2-4-6 style rule task, 11 LLMs mostly proposed tests that fit their current guess, success ranged 6 to 78%, and counterexample prompting raised average discovery from 42% to 56% (Think-in-Opposites helped in all 11 scenarios). Thinking mode raised success without raising the disconfirming-test ratio. Instruction only; no structural arm.
agent_test: Compare a counterexample instruction with a forced step that writes the test most likely to refute the leader and runs it.

claim: Debate-style and role-based multi-agent setups give small or no gains over self-consistency at equal compute on general reasoning (not reliably better than CoT or SC in five methods x nine benchmarks; +1.3 to +2.7 points on MMLU-Pro for debate and mixture-of-agents). Role design and model mix matter more than role count. No diagnosis test has a matched control.
agent_test: Same-token control on fault tasks (see K13).

claim: Instruction-level debiasing is model-dependent and can over-correct: when asked to fix their own earlier decisions, Llama-2-13b changed 52.1% and Llama-2-7b 39.9% (GPT-3.5 5.2%, GPT-4 17.5%) with no ground truth to show gain; few-shot counterfactual debiasing pushed outputs to extremes. A structural check has not been compared head to head.
agent_test: Compare 'be careful about bias' vs evidence-gated change rule (switch only when a named new observation favors the alternative) on staged cases; score regressions and missed updates.

claim: What can be confirmed for Rasmussen and Morris and Rouse is thin: Rasmussen and Jensen 1974 (abstract) report fixation and repetition of routines after failure in skilled electronics repairers; Rasmussen's topographic vs symptomatic search split is confirmed secondhand; Morris and Rouse 1985 (abstract) cover training and explicit guidance with no hypothesis count; a 1985 Georgia Tech aid displayed hypotheses to offload working memory. None gives how many hypotheses operators hold or how they discard them.
agent_test: Do not cite Rasmussen or Morris and Rouse for a hypothesis count. Primary texts remain unopened (publisher and repository bot walls).

claim: A prompted-differential list length of 7 to 10 is reachable by a trained 7B model when length is not penalized (mean 9.56 diagnoses with binary reward), with differential accuracy 62.4 vs 65.2 at 8.66 and 57.2 at 7.25; broad lists led to redundant test ordering. Training result, not spontaneous prompted behavior; no study varies requested N (3, 6, 12) for a prompted model.
agent_test: Prompt for N = 3, 6, 12 hypotheses on the same fault items; plot true-cause coverage, top-1, tokens.
